newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on short covering rebound.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on short covering rebound.

text.p: KCBT wheat futures closed higher on a late short-covering rebound after the sharp drop in the market Tuesday, traders said.
The market was under pressure most of the day on overall good crop weather for wheat in the United States.

There were rains forecast for the dry wheat growing areas of Kansas and Nebraska, traders said. That region of the U.S. Great Plains has been drier than normal and the moisture will help boost crop prospects, they said.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed three cents per bushel higher to one lower, with July up 2-1/2 at $4.13-3/4.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the KCBT at 24.150 million bushels, below the 38.605 million traded Tuesday.
